providers.selectedSource: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json OIDC session; when access expiry is within 60 seconds or the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, refresh_token grant at fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token and atomic same-file rotation, then one proxy retry; primary cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits; only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, bearer-only POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same session bearer and a 6-second timeout
providers.sourceStatusReason: The Grok CLI owner session and CLI-proxy credits endpoint remain primary. Unlike CodexBar, which is only a reference for credits behavior and does not directly refresh OAuth, Token Jar performs the user-approved narrow renewal: an OIDC access token expiring within 60 seconds, or one rejected by the first proxy request with 401/403, is renewed once through the official fixed token endpoint after exact issuer and selected client/scope checks; the rotated session is atomically preserved to the same owner file before one proxy retry. Only a successful proxy snapshot with unknown usage may trigger the existing same-session bearer-only gRPC-web billing fallback. Proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity remain authoritative; web billing supplies usage only. Token Jar never imports browser cookies, uses Grok ACP stdio or a CLI subprocess, offers manual-token UI, calls the xAI Management prepaid-balance API, or caches tokens in Keychain.
providers.rejectedAlternative: Browser-cookie imports, Grok ACP stdio, CLI subprocess or interactive automation, manual-token UI, local-session estimates, xAI Management API/prepaid-balance calls, Keychain token caches, backups, other secret stores, and arbitrary credential copying remain prohibited. The older Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing probe returned JSON-RPC -32601 (method-not-found) on official Grok 1.0.13.
providers.credentialOwner: Grok CLI, with user-approved Token Jar renewal of the selected OIDC entry
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json; Token Jar may atomically replace only that same file after a successful official refresh_token grant, preserving the optional rotated refresh token and updated expires_at; no backup, copy, or other secret store
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json through the Grok-scoped session capability; require issuer https://auth.x.ai and exact agreement between the selected client/scope suffix and the entry's non-empty oidc_client_id

When expires_at is within 60 seconds, or only after the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, POST a refresh_token grant to fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with public-client authentication, no cookies, and no redirects

Once renewal starts, hold a bounded token-free lock shared only by Token Jar processes across the current-file reread, HTTP rotation, conflict comparison, and same-file persistence; preserve the response's optional rotated refresh token and updated expiry in the selected entry, prefer an observably newer external session, and replace through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. Observer cancellation does not interrupt the shared transaction: a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit; cancellation before renewal starts aborts. Grok CLI is not assumed to honor the lock.
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with the selected ephemeral bearer; after 401/403 renewal, retry this proxy exactly once

Only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same selected bearer, a 5-byte empty gRPC-web data frame (00 00 00 00 00), no cookies, and a 6-second timeout

Preserve proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity; adopt a published web percentage, or an omitted proto3 scalar as zero only for a structurally complete response with a recognized current weekly/monthly period containing the refresh time; otherwise retain unknown, including a failed fallback
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row on-demand used/cap ratio under the credits quota
Display only the selected auth entry's optional email in memory; never infer identity from another entry or token
providers.liveValidation: Historical evidence: on 2026-09-07 a current-host read-only probe reproduced HTTP 200 proxy credits with no creditUsagePercent, onDemandUsed/onDemandCap both zero, and currentPeriod present; the production Swift adapter plus URLSessionNetworkClient returned used 0%, remaining 100%, and preserved proxy reset through a validated active-period proto3 implicit zero from bearer-only web billing. The 97 package tests reported then cover the pre-renewal implementation. Current evidence: 117 Swift package tests, 33 app unit tests, 13 release-tool tests, Provider I/O audit, forbidden FileTimestamp API check, independent integration review, and rotation review pass 2 passed. A token-safe current-host production GrokOAuthSessionProvider probe on 2026-09-11 forced exactly one renewal with rejectedAccessToken set to the current token, then fetched usage through the real GrokAdapter: access token changed, refresh token rotated, saved token matched the returned session, expiry was in the future, file mode was 0600, noncredential metadata was preserved, usage fetch succeeded with one quota and available usage percentage, and account identity matched the session. No secret was printed or copied. This does not prove a naturally expired-token event, real HTTP 401/403 injection, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, packaged final release, another OS, CI, or notarization.
providers.mutationRisk: The only credential mutation allowed is successful Grok renewal written atomically to the same ~/.grok/auth.json through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. A bounded token-free lock covers reread, HTTP rotation, comparison, and persistence among Token Jar processes; once renewal starts it settles despite observer cancellation, after which a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit, while pre-start cancellation aborts. Comparison detects observable external rotation and prefers a newer session but cannot close the final rename window against an uncooperative concurrent Grok CLI writer; the lock is not claimed to be CLI-honored. No backup, other secret store, cookie import, Management API fallback, or unrelated source-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: live-validate a naturally near-expiry event, real proxy HTTP 401/403 renewal, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, missing/revoked versus network-error recovery, and the packaged final candidate on supported OS versions; complete CI, signing, and notarization evidence

providers.surface: Cursor individual account usage summary and billing-cycle quota blocks
providers.selectedSource: Read-only Cursor.app state.vscdb session plus cursor.com/api/usage-summary
providers.sourceStatusReason: Cursor documents the usage surface but not the local session layout or usage-summary endpoint. Token Jar follows the current CodexBar behavior as a reference, reads the Cursor-owned SQLite value in place with immutable=1 and no persistence or refresh, and fails closed on expiry or schema drift.
providers.credentialPersistence: Cursor-owned state.vscdb; Token Jar does not persist, copy, write, or refresh the JWT
tokenTankIO: Open only Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb with O_NOFOLLOW, verify the opened descriptor identity, bind immutable=1 SQLite to that descriptor, and query only ItemTable cursorAuth/accessToken and cursorAuth/cachedEmail
Require a canonical token envelope, bounded allowed subject, and unexpired timestamp; use it only in an ephemeral owner-session cookie whose authority is decided by cursor.com/api/usage-summary
Expose individual and team usage blocks, plan breakdowns, and percentages independently with opaque identities
Display optional cachedEmail from the same SQLite read in memory only; absent or invalid email does not suppress usage
providers.liveValidation: Immutable exact-key read preserved all tracked main/WAL/SHM facts and the owner session returned the expected usage-summary root and individual plan/onDemand blocks; ordinary mode=ro was rejected after it changed SQLite metadata.
providers.mutationRisk: Immutable SQLite ignores active WAL state rather than touching shared-memory metadata; an older/expired checkpointed token fails closed. No browser import, token cache, copy, refresh, or external-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the descriptor-bound immutable read, sanitized schema, and exact owner path through the final frozen candidate
